title: Peacock raises prices by 18 percent after becoming profitable
gist: Peacock raised prices for the fourth time in four years (Premium up to $13, Premium Plus to $20) right after posting its first quarterly profit ($189M adjusted EBITDA in Q2 2026), even as NBCUniversal shoulders heavy live-sports spending like a $2.5B/year NBA deal.

insights.claim: Peacock turned its first quarterly profit in Q2 2026 with $189 million in adjusted EBITDA, as subscription revenue rose over 50 percent and advertising revenue nearly 70 percent, and it added 2 million subscribers to reach 48 million.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: A late-to-profit streamer crossing breakeven while raising prices signals the industry's pivot from growth to margin—watch subscriber retention against hikes.
insights.locator: The streaming service turned its first quarterly profit

insights.claim: Peacock raised prices for the fourth consecutive year, with Premium going from $11 to $13 and Premium Plus from $17 to $20, an 18 percent hike immediately after reaching profitability.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Serial annual hikes suggest pricing has become the primary profit lever; a template for streaming monetization and churn risk.
insights.locator: For the fourth time in four years

insights.claim: NBCUniversal must keep Peacock profitable amid heavy live-events spending, including an 11-year deal paying $2.5 billion a year for about 50 exclusive NBA games plus Sunday Night Football and Premier League rights.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Massive sports-rights commitments pressure streaming margins and drive the price hikes; quarterly profits will swing with content calendars.
insights.locator: NBCUniversal must also keep Peacock profitable
